pr_title: Check extension for latest version when executed
pr_body:
<!--
  Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!
  To reference an open issue, please write this in your description: `Fixes #NUMBER`
-->
Fixes #8183 

This PR applies the same approach used for checking and informing users of new `gh` releases to extensions when they are executed.  The benefit being that GitHub CLI users can be notified about new versions as they use the extension without putting that effort onto GitHub CLI extension authors.

> [!NOTE]
> This is initially created as a draft for feedback from core maintainers and the community before investing more effort to polish and complete the work.

### Demo

```shell
andrewfeller@Andrews-MacBook-Pro cli % gh ext install dlvhdr/gh-dash --pin v4.6.0
✓ Installed extension dlvhdr/gh-dash
✓ Pinned extension at v4.6.0
```

```shell
andrewfeller@Andrews-MacBook-Pro cli % ./bin/gh dash

A new release of dash is available: 4.6.0 → 4.7.0
To upgrade, run: gh extension upgrade dash --force
https://github.com/dlvhdr/gh-dash
```

### Open questions

1. **How frequently do we check for new extension releases?**

   The `gh` version checking only happens at minimum every 24 hours, relying upon information in XDG state directory on when it was last checked.  If the similar approach is desired here, then either the existing state file will be expanded OR `gh` maintains state information per extension.

   ```shell
   % cat ~/.local/state/gh/state.yml 
   checked_for_update_at: 2024-11-02T11:07:12.423561-04:00
   latest_release:
       version: v2.60.1
       url: https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.60.1
       publishedat: 2024-10-25T17:15:00Z
   ```

1. **What degree of testing is sufficient?**

   Being based on the existing behavior as Cobra command hooks, it is possible but want to solicit feedback before investing the time to understand any changes to the implementation.
pr_comments:
After taking a second pass at these changes, I'll admit I'm second guessing how much we attempt to apply the same update caching logic used below around `gh`.  I'll explain my reasoning below but here is the code in question:

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/215e4f440f56a0652e5c0f64614b64edcf1da1bc/internal/update/update.go#L22-L111

### Reasoning

The `gh` update checking logic is simple and straightforward:

1. `gh` has releases so we can make API calls to pull information
2. We're only checking a single GitHub repo for releases

Contrast that with extensions:

1. There are [3 types of extensions with very different mechanisms](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/215e4f440f56a0652e5c0f64614b64edcf1da1bc/pkg/cmd/extension/extension.go#L88-L221) around version handling
   1. Local extension
   2. Remote script-based extension
   3. Remote binary-based extension
1. Local + remote binary-based extensions have [manifests](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/215e4f440f56a0652e5c0f64614b64edcf1da1bc/pkg/cmd/extension/manager.go#L203-L211) similar to `gh` update state information however not exactly the same
1. These manifests are are the domain of the [extension manager](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/215e4f440f56a0652e5c0f64614b64edcf1da1bc/pkg/cmd/extension/manager.go#L323-L335), possibly requiring a major refactor if we want to cache information per extension

With all of that said, I think there's enough done on the PR to bring it out of draft for further feedback.

> I like it! I'd ship the version-check as-is, I think, but you were looking for feedback so I've left a couple of questions.
> 
> Additionally, it's not clear to me what the inclusion of `licenses.tmpl` and `licenses.yml` files are for, here. Can you explain them to me?

I'll be honest: I have no idea how that landed here.

issue_context.title: Check for new version of extension when invoked, print message notifying user of upgrade
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

GitHub CLI extension authors want to ensure users are running the newest version of extensions. 
 Like the GitHub CLI checks for updates every 24 hours when invoked, the GitHub CLI could perform the same logic when an extension command is invoked.

This would ensure GitHub CLI extension users knew about potentially necessary or valuable updates while minimizing the amount of effort on extension authors from reimplementing the logic already within GitHub CLI.

### Proposed solution

1. Refactor the update logic within `cmd/gh/main.go` to be reusable

   https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/64f4660ec71a46a7c7089ca81c0366de4cc9b000/cmd/gh/main.go#L59-L68

   https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/64f4660ec71a46a7c7089ca81c0366de4cc9b000/cmd/gh/main.go#L165-L182

1. Enhance dynamic extension command generation to ensure extension release is checked independently of one another or GitHub CLI

   https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/64f4660ec71a46a7c7089ca81c0366de4cc9b000/pkg/cmd/root/root.go#L170-L175

1. Ensure latest release information logic supports GitHub Enterprise users

   https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/64f4660ec71a46a7c7089ca81c0366de4cc9b000/internal/update/update.go#L58-L80

cc: @samcoe @nickfyson 

### Additional context

I was originally attempting to move the `internal/update` package to `cli/go-gh`, requiring the standardization on its `api` clients for the function.  After talking with @samcoe about the process going from `cli/cli` api clients to `cli/go-gh` api clients, Sam's suggestion of having GitHub CLI do the checking would benefit all extensions without effort.
comments: Realizing there is duplication between this and #5964.  I believe the thoughts here echo those made by @vilmibm about not wanting to impact the experience, primarily focusing on notifying the user the extension has a newer release available.
would this approach work for non-Go based extensions?

> would this approach work for non-Go based extensions?

@dylan-smith : personally, I would like some way that we could detect this for either binary and script based extensions.  I'm not sure how this would work for extensions that are locally installed; likely nothing happens to them.  The main challenge I can see is that script based extensions are cloned repositories even when installing via a pinned tag.

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/20baccfa85d15963eb1ab4f750da0da37b0af7f5/pkg/cmd/extension/manager.go#L211-L237

```shell
$ gh extension install andyfeller/gh-repo-export --pin v1.2.0 
Cloning into '/Users/andyfeller/.local/share/gh/extensions/gh-repo-export'...
remote: Enumerating objects: 82, done.
remote: Counting objects: 100% (82/82), done.
remote: Compressing objects: 100% (63/63), done.
remote: Total 82 (delta 34), reused 47 (delta 17), pack-reused 0
Receiving objects: 100% (82/82), 23.46 KiB | 5.86 MiB/s, done.

$ gh extension list

```

Just wanted to officially 'plus 1' this issue, as having this functionality provided by the default CLI would enable us to take the duplicated functionality out of `github/gh-autofix`. 🙂

Also wanted to comment as a reminder to myself of the need for some coordination to avoid users getting double-notified (at least not _too_ many times 😆).

While discussing this with @samcoe today, we largely reaffirmed initial points above in that it made sense to add this logic specifically to the commands for extensions and that we would need to maintain state information for the extension.

The only unanswered question is: **do we manage cached release information for extensions differently than GitHub CLI?**

1. The GitHub CLI checks at the least every 24 hours whether there is a new version available and caches that information under state:

   ```shell
   $ cat ~/.local/state/gh/state.yml 
   checked_for_update_at: 2023-11-13T08:07:36.475011-05:00
   latest_release:
       version: v2.38.0
       url: https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.38.0
       publishedat: 2023-11-01T10:52:41Z
   ```

1. The GitHub CLI manages extensions under data directory:

   ```shell
   $ cat ~/.local/share/gh/extensions/gh-copilot/manifest.yml 
   owner: github
   name: gh-copilot
   host: github.com
   tag: v0.5.3-beta
   ispinned: false
   path: /Users/andyfeller/.local/share/gh/extensions/gh-copilot/gh-copilot
   ```

This division is based upon [XDG Base Directory Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html), which causes us to question which trade off we're willing to make:

1. Treat the extension release information like state and maintain in `$XDG_STATE_HOME` directory, separate from the extensions themselves and their manifests
   - Pro: provides a single space on disk for all state information
   - Con: spreads information about extension all over the place

1. Couple the extension release information like extension artifacts and maintain in `$XDG_DATA_HOME` directory, spreading release information in multiple places
   - Pro: makes cleaning up an extension straightforward, delete the directory
   - Con: spreads release information all over the place

Between these 2 approaches, it is arguable that the latter is more important the former.

Not to de-rail the discussion here too much, but I just opened a new semi-related issue that proposes adding a `gh extensions outdated` command, and it would seem that the update check+cached versions discussion here would work well for that feature too:

- https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/8327

🤔 Something about this being an IIFE (instantly invoked functional expression) is giving me pause... That said, I'm not sure I've ever seen a goroutine created with a named function. Is that the convention?

Either way, I know you're interested in testing, and if this IIFE was extracted to a named function with its dependencies injected (`updateMessageChan`, `extensionReleaseInfo`, and `ext`) testing it would be pretty simple. It's a lot harder to test it here, as written.
Just updated the PR with tests.  I don't think there's a lot of value testing channel handling behavior so much as if we're emitting the expected messages on standard error.
Yeah, I agree... I didn't know the mocks existed for extensions already, so the tests for this are more straight forward than I anticipated ❤️ Definitely think you've nailed the tests
This doesn't seem to be used in any of the test cases. Should we remove it?
Great catch, that's totally an oversight on my part and we should probably expand the `wantStderr` in the various test cases to check the url!
